newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-HKMA official says HK dollar link to remain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-HKMA official says HK dollar link to remain.

text.p: Hong Kong's currency link to the U.S. dollar would survive unchanged after the return of the British colony to Chinese sovereignty in July, an official with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Thursday.

"The Hong Kong dollar linkage system has been in place for more than 14 years now - it has weathered quite a lot of shocks," Raymond Li, HKMA's banking policy executive director, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
"We are now in a better position than ever to keep that system in place," he added.
Li was speaking at a derivatives conference here.
Under the fixed exchange rate system, the Hong Kong dollar has been pegged at 7.80 to one U.S. dollar since 1983.
As the colony's de facto central bank, the HKMA focuses on banking supervision and protecting the peg.
Li said he did not expect any depreciation in the currency after July 1, when China assumes sovereignty of Hong Kong.
"The pressure has been on the stronger side of the link for a long time now," Li told RFTV.
"I don't expect any depreciation at all."
Li said China's leadership was fully supportive of the continuation of the peg.
